content:
Rachel Kim: Kicking off a quick thread to lock the *pilot handoff checklist* for regulated accounts. We keep getting pulled in late and missing context. For CS to take over from SE/Sales, we need the below completed + linked in the account doc. Adding owners + due dates so it’s not hand-wavy.

Rachel Kim: **CS Handoff Checklist (Regulated Pilot → Implementation)**
1) **Success criteria + SLOs (final)**
- Latency target (p50/p95), throughput, availability assumptions, error budget
- Any “must have” compliance requirements (audit logs, retention, residency)
Owner: @Evan Scott (SE) + @Liam O'Rourke (TAM)
Due: Wed EOD (5/14)

2) **Environment + architecture (what is actually deployed)**
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) + region
- High-level diagram (ok to be a screenshot) + networking notes (egress allowlist, TLS termination)
Owner: @Simran Kaur (SA) / @Fatima Noor (SE)
Due: Wed EOD (5/14)

3) **Dashboards + monitoring**
- Links to Redwood Console dashboards used during pilot (latency, errors, token usage, cost)
- Any custom metrics / traces (and where they live)
- Alerting thresholds used in pilot (if any)
Owner: @Evan Scott
Due: Thu noon (5/15)

4) **Runbooks (minimum viable)**
- “What to do when latency spikes” (batching/caching knobs, scaling path, who to page)
- “What to do when outputs regress” (model pinning, rollback/fallback policy)
- “Audit log export / evidence pack asks” (what we can share + where)
Owner: @Markus Klein (SE lead) + @Fatima Noor
Due: Fri EOD (5/16)

5) **Access + comms**
- Who at customer is primary/backup + escalation
- Shared Slack channel/email thread link
- Redwood internal channel + who’s still engaged from Eng/Sec
- Confirm CS has access to the environment (Console org, any Private admin creds process)
Owner: @Rachel Kim + @Jasmine Liu
Due: Thu EOD (5/15)

6) **Open risks + blockers**
- Security questionnaire outstanding items, procurement timeline assumptions
- Known product gaps / workarounds agreed with customer
Owner: @Stephanie Nguyen (Sales) + @Liam O'Rourke
Due: Thu EOD (5/15)

Rachel Kim: If we have this, CS can run the rollout/QBR without pinging SE every 2 hours. If we don’t, we end up re-learning everything.

Jasmine Liu: +1. Can we make “SLOs” more explicit? For the Northbridge-style pilots, I want *written* agreement on what’s in vs out (eg. “PHI/PCI data not used in pilot” / “synthetic data only”).

Rachel Kim: good call. Adding under #1: data boundaries + dataset notes (synthetic vs prod, retention, any redactions). @Evan Scott can you include that in the SLO/success criteria doc?

Evan Scott: yep. For Northbridge we already have the mutual action plan doc w/ targets; I’ll pull into a single handoff page and drop links here.

Liam O'Rourke: For access/comms: please include who owns the customer’s on-call side (some of these pilots have “platform team” + “security team” and neither wants to be first line). Also need timezone coverage.

Rachel Kim: +1. Will add “customer on-call / coverage hours” under #5.

Markus Klein: For runbooks, can we keep it lightweight but actionable. I can template:
- symptoms
- quick checks
- mitigation knobs (what we can change safely)
- escalation path
I’ll draft a Google doc template and share.

Fatima Noor: re: audit log export asks, we should be careful w/ wording. Some prospects keep asking for “full request/response logging” which we do *not* want to imply by default. We can document what fields exist + how to export, but keep it aligned to Security FAQ.

Rachel Kim: agreed. Keep it “audit events + admin actions + access logs” wording unless Security signs off. We can link the internal Security FAQ / evidence pack index.

Simran Kaur: On architecture diagrams: I can do a standard Private/VPC reference and annotate deltas per account (eg, customer-managed KMS, log sink). Will post a screenshot and a short paragraph.

Stephanie Nguyen: Sales side: I’ll make sure “procurement assumptions” + “next commercial step” is included. Also: if there’s any pilot credits/discount terms, CS should see the guardrails so we don’t promise extra.

Rachel Kim: thank you. Please include where the term lives (email thread ok) so we don’t have to hunt.

Evan Scott: Quick question: where do we want the final handoff page to live? Confluence vs Drive? I’ve been doing Drive during pilot.

Jasmine Liu: Drive is fine for speed, but drop the link into the HubSpot record + the CS handoff section so it doesn’t get lost.

Rachel Kim: +1. For now: Drive doc for the handoff page, linked in HubSpot + pinned in the shared Slack channel. If this becomes standard, we’ll templatize in Confluence.

Markus Klein: :thumbsup: I’ll have the runbook template by tomorrow morning.

Fatima Noor: I’ll add a small section to runbook template: “Security review FAQs we’ve answered” + “evidence already shared” so CS doesn’t re-send things.

Rachel Kim: perfect. I’ll check in Thu AM on status. If anything slips, please flag in-thread early vs day-of handoff.

Rachel Kim: (reaction summary) ✅ owners set, dates set. Next step: @Evan Scott post draft handoff page link when ready.
